adults.title: Receive, and the Lord Will Give More
adults.big_idea: Conference keeps blessing us after it ends: as we study and ponder the talks prayerfully and act in faith on them, the Lord promises to give us more.
adults.objective: Learners will choose one talk from this conference to study prayerfully this week and write down one way they will act in faith on what they learn.
prepare: Read President Oaks’s closing remarks (seven short paragraphs) and 2 Nephi 28:30.
Write four words on the board: STUDY, PONDER, PRAY, ACT.
Bring a slip of paper and a pencil for each person.
Have the list of talks from this conference ready to show or pass around (Gospel Library or the conference issue of the Liahona).

segments.name: What has stayed with you?
steps: After the opening prayer, hand out paper. Give one quiet minute to write one thing from this general conference that has stayed with them: a phrase, a feeling, a prompting.
Invite each person to turn to a neighbor and share what they wrote and why they think it stayed.
Explain that today’s lesson comes from the very short message President Oaks gave at the close of conference, and that it is about what we do next.
questions: What from this conference has stayed with you, and why do you think it did?

segments.name: The invitation in his words
steps: Ask someone to read aloud the first two paragraphs of the closing remarks (T37.01 and T37.02 in key quotes). Ask the class to listen for what President Oaks says conference did for us and what he invites us to do now.
Point to the four words on the board. Form groups of three and give each group one or two of the words. Ask: what does this word add that simply listening once does not?
After three minutes, hear one sentence from each group.
Check for understanding: ask one person to restate the whole invitation in their own words.
questions: President Oaks says conference inspired us to focus on the teachings of Jesus Christ and His Father’s plan. Where did you feel that focus?
What is the difference between reading a talk and studying it? Between thinking about it and pondering it prayerfully?
Why do you think he says to act “in faith” rather than only to act?

segments.name: The promise
steps: Read again the last sentence of T37.02: the Lord’s promise that He gives more to the one who receives.
In pairs, read 2 Nephi 28:30. Ask pairs to look for two things: how the Lord gives, and what happens to those who decide they have enough.
Read Moroni 10:3–5 together and ask what it adds about how to receive truth from God.

Share President Uchtdorf’s words from this conference (aligned quotes) and invite two or three people to answer the questions below from their own experience. Let silence do its work before you speak.
questions: When has acting on one small thing you learned opened the way for the Lord to teach you more?
What does receiving look like on an ordinary weekday?

segments.name: Looking forward to the house of the Lord
steps: Ask someone to read paragraphs three through five of the closing remarks. Have the class listen for the date and for whom the Church is welcoming.

Note what President Oaks said: on April 5, 2027, the doors of the Salt Lake Temple will open to the public, the first such opening since 1893, and the world is welcome in person or virtually. He pointed us to TempleSquare.org and the Temple Square app, and to a video series called Dedicate.
Read Elder Gong’s words (aligned quotes). Give thirty seconds of quiet for each person to think of one name.
questions: President Oaks says we are welcoming the world. Who is one person you could welcome, in person or virtually?
What would help you feel ready to extend that welcome?

segments.name: Choose one talk and make a plan
steps: Show or pass around the list of conference talks. Invite a silent prayer, then ask each person to choose one talk to study first. Suggest simple ways to choose: a title that speaks to a question they are carrying, a message during which they felt something, or the talk they wrote about at the start of class.

On their paper, have them write four lines: the talk; when and where they will study it; one question they will pray about as they ponder it; and a blank line labeled What I will do, to fill in after they study.
Invite them to read James 1:22 silently and then tell a neighbor their plan.

segments.name: His blessing and testimony
steps: Read aloud President Oaks’s blessing (T37.06) and his testimony (T37.07). Ask the class to listen as people the blessing was given to.
Add your own brief testimony of the Savior and of His promise to give more to those who receive.
Follow up: tell the class that next week you will begin by asking two or three people what they received from the talk they chose and what they did about it.

key_quotes.text: the great messages of this conference and the Spirit of the Lord have inspired all of us to concentrate our worship, focus our learning, and unite our testimonies on the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ and His Father’s plan for our eternal increase and joy.

As the talks of this conference are published, we invite all to study and ponder them prayerfully and to act in faith on the principles they explain. The Lord has promised, “Unto him that receiveth I will give more.”
As we now go forward, we invoke the blessings of the Lord on you and your families, blessings of peace and contentment. And we bless your service of the Lord Jesus Christ in these challenging times.
Truth is to be found here—truth about the teachings of the Lord and truth about the covenant path that will lead us to our destiny, the destiny desired by our Heavenly Father.

scriptures.use: The source of the promise President Oaks quotes. Read in pairs; look for how the Lord gives and what happens to those who say they have enough.
Read together in the promise segment; ask what it adds about how to receive truth from God.
Read silently while making a plan; let it move each person from hearing a talk to doing something about it.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Uchtdorf
aligned_quotes.text: Spiritual growth is rarely dramatic at the beginning.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Gong
aligned_quotes.text: let us celebrate and treasure even more the spiritual blessings temples bring

invitations.text: As the talks of this conference are published, we invite all to study and ponder them prayerfully and to act in faith on the principles they explain.
Join us at TempleSquare.org or through the Temple Square app to learn more.

takeaways: Conference is meant to be studied, pondered prayerfully and acted on, not only heard.
The Lord promises to give more to those who receive what He has already given.
The doors of the Salt Lake Temple will open to the public on April 5, 2027, and we can help welcome the world.
act: Study the one talk you chose, at the time you wrote down, with a prayer before and after.
Fill in the blank line on your paper with one thing you will do, and do it before next Sunday.
Visit TempleSquare.org or the Temple Square app and decide whom you will welcome to learn more with you.
Tell one person at home what you received from the talk you studied.
music: As I Search the Holy Scriptures
We Thank Thee, O God, for a Prophet
adapt: At home: sit around the table, let each person choose a talk, and post the plans on the refrigerator; report at the next home evening.
Large class: skip the groups of three and have neighbors discuss just one of the four words; take only two comments per question.
Short on time: keep the invitation, the promise, and the choose-and-plan segments; read the temple paragraphs aloud without discussion.

youth.title: Conference Isn’t Over
youth.big_idea: The Lord gives more to those who receive what He has already given, so what we do with conference after it ends matters.
youth.objective: Youth will pick one conference talk, make a simple plan to study, ponder, pray and act on it this week, and write one true sentence of their own testimony.
prepare: Read President Oaks’s closing remarks (seven short paragraphs) and 2 Nephi 28:30.
Bring paper and pens, a clear cup, a small pitcher of water, and a bowl or towel.
Ask youth to have Gospel Library or their scriptures ready; have a printed list of conference talks for anyone without a phone.
Write on the board: STUDY, PONDER, PRAY, ACT.

segments.name: Sixty-second recall
steps: As soon as the prayer ends, put youth in teams of two or three with one sheet of paper. Give exactly sixty seconds to list everything they remember from this general conference: speakers, stories, phrases, feelings.
Count the lists and cheer the longest one. Then ask the question below and take two or three honest answers.
questions: If we do nothing else, how much of this list will we still have in a month?

segments.name: Find the invitation
steps: Have everyone open President Oaks’s closing remarks from the last session. Tell them it is the shortest talk of the conference: seven paragraphs.
Challenge: in the second paragraph, find the things he invites us to do with the conference talks and the promise from the Lord that follows. First to find them reads the paragraph aloud.
Match what they found to the four words on the board.
Check for understanding: ask someone to say the invitation in the words they would use with a friend.
questions: Why isn’t hearing a talk once enough?
Which of the four is hardest for you, honestly, and why?

segments.name: The open cup
steps: Hold the cup over the bowl with your hand covering the top. Ask a youth to pour a little water; it runs off. Uncover the cup and pour again. Ask what changed. The water was the same; the cup was open.
In pairs, read 2 Nephi 28:30. Look for who receives more and what happens to those who say they have enough.
Read the promise as President Oaks quoted it: “Unto him that receiveth I will give more.”
Share President Uchtdorf’s words (aligned quotes) and ask the questions below.
questions: What does a covered cup look like in real life? What does an open one look like?
When has doing one small thing you were taught led to understanding more?

segments.name: First pick
steps: Give two minutes to scroll the list of talks from this conference and choose a first pick: the one talk they will study first. Ways to choose: a title that fits a question they have right now, a talk during which they felt something, or one a parent or leader mentioned.
Each tells a partner the pick and the reason.
Read James 1:5 silently. Then have each youth write one real question to pray about while they study their talk.
On the same paper, write when and where they will study it, and leave a line labeled What I will do.

segments.name: The doors will open
steps: Ask a youth to read paragraphs three through five of the closing remarks. Have everyone listen for a date and two numbers.

Review what President Oaks said: on April 5, 2027, the doors of the Salt Lake Temple will open to the public for the first time since 1893, which is 134 years. The world is welcome in person or virtually, and there is a video series called Dedicate and a virtual tour to come.
Each youth drafts a two-sentence message they could send a friend, inviting them to look at TempleSquare.org or the Temple Square app together. They decide later whether to send it.
questions: President Oaks says we are welcoming the world. Who is one friend you would want to welcome?

segments.name: One true sentence
steps: Read President Oaks’s testimony in the last paragraph. Ask youth to notice the phrase “Truth is to be found here” and what two kinds of truth he names.
Read Elder Caussé’s words about testimony (aligned quotes).
Give one quiet minute for each youth to write a single sentence about something they know or are coming to believe. Invite a few volunteers to read theirs. No one is required to.

segments.name: Blessing and challenge
steps: Read President Oaks’s blessing in paragraph six. Point out that he blessed them and their families with peace and contentment, and blessed their service of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Give the challenge: study your first pick this week, pray about your question, and do one thing because of it.
Follow up: next week, open class by having each youth share one line from their talk and the one thing they did.

key_quotes.text: we invite all to study and ponder them prayerfully and to act in faith on the principles they explain. The Lord has promised, “Unto him that receiveth I will give more.”
On April 5, 2027, the temple doors will open to the public—the first such opening since 1893, 134 years ago.
Truth is to be found here—truth about the teachings of the Lord and truth about the covenant path that will lead us to our destiny, the destiny desired by our Heavenly Father.

scriptures.use: The source of the promise President Oaks quotes. Read in pairs after the cup demonstration; look for who receives more and what happens to those who say they have enough.
Read silently before writing a question to pray about while studying the chosen talk.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Uchtdorf
aligned_quotes.text: Spiritual growth is rarely dramatic at the beginning.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Caussé
aligned_quotes.text: It need not be long, eloquent, or dramatic—it only needs to be true.

invitations.text: As the talks of this conference are published, we invite all to study and ponder them prayerfully and to act in faith on the principles they explain.
Join us at TempleSquare.org or through the Temple Square app to learn more.

takeaways: The prophet invited me to study, ponder, pray about and act on the conference talks.
The Lord gives more to those who receive what He has already given.
Truth is found in the restored gospel of Jesus Christ, and I can say what I know in one true sentence.
act: Study your first-pick talk this week, with your question written at the top of your notes.
Do one specific thing because of that talk and write it on the blank line.
Look at TempleSquare.org or the Temple Square app, and send your invitation to a friend if it feels right.
Share your one true sentence with someone at home.
music: We Thank Thee, O God, for a Prophet
adapt: At home or with one or two youth: do the recall list together, and have a parent choose a talk and make a plan too.
No phones or no water: use printed copies of the talk and the list of talks, and show the cup idea with a ball tossed to open hands and then to folded arms.
Short on time: keep Find the invitation, The open cup, and First pick.

children.title: Open Hands, Open Heart
children.big_idea: When I listen to the prophet and do what I learn, Heavenly Father gives me more.
children.objective: Children will show the four actions the prophet invited us to do with conference (study, think, pray, do) and choose one good thing to do this week.
prepare: Read President Oaks’s closing remarks and 2 Nephi 28:30.
Bring a soft ball, paper, and crayons.
Find a picture of President Oaks and a picture of the Salt Lake Temple in Gospel Library or the meetinghouse library.
Think of one simple thing you remember from this conference to share in a sentence.

segments.name: Sing and meet the prophet
steps: After the prayer, sing the chorus of Follow the Prophet while marching in place.
Show the picture of President Oaks. Say: at the very end of general conference, President Oaks gave us a short message. Today we will learn what he asked us to do.

segments.name: Four actions game
steps: Tell the children that President Oaks invited everyone to study the conference talks, think about them with prayer, and do what they teach.
Teach four motions. Study: hold hands open like a book. Think: touch a finger to your head. Pray: fold your arms. Do: march in place.
Call out the words in order, then mix them up and go faster. Let a child be the caller.
End by saying together: I can listen and do.

segments.name: Open hands
steps: Stand the children in a circle. Ask one child to fold their arms tight, and gently pretend to hand them the ball. Ask: can you take it with your arms folded like that?
Now ask the child to hold out open hands, and give them the ball. Pass or roll the ball around the circle so every child receives it with open hands.

Say: President Oaks told us a promise from the Lord. Read it slowly: “Unto him that receiveth I will give more.” Explain that to receive means to take in what Heavenly Father gives us, like open hands take the ball.
Say together: I can listen and do.
questions: How can we show Heavenly Father that our hearts are open?

segments.name: The temple doors will open
steps: Show the picture of the Salt Lake Temple. Invite the children to stand tall with hands together above their heads like a spire.
Tell them: President Oaks said that on April 5, 2027, the doors of the Salt Lake Temple will open to the public, and that the Church is welcoming the world. The temple is the house of the Lord.
Sing I Love to See the Temple.

segments.name: Draw the temple
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Invite them to draw the temple with its doors open and to draw themselves beside it.
As they draw, walk around and ask each child to tell you about the picture.
Ask the question below and let several children answer.
questions: How do you feel when you see a temple?

segments.name: One thing I will do
steps: Tell the children one simple thing you remember from conference, in one sentence. Ask what they remember: a song, a story, how they felt.

Explain that the prophet invited us to keep learning from conference. Suggest simple choices: listen to one conference talk or story with someone at home, say a prayer about what I heard, or do one kind thing I learned about.
Have each child turn the paper over and draw the one thing they choose. Help younger children by writing a few words for them.

segments.name: A blessing and a testimony
steps: Ask the children to sit quietly with arms folded. Tell them that President Oaks blessed us and our families with peace. Whisper together: peace.
Tell them he ended with his testimony that this is the restored gospel of Jesus Christ. Share your own short testimony that Heavenly Father loves them and gives more to those who listen and do.
Do the four motions one last time. Follow up: ask the children to bring back their paper next week and tell what they did.

key_quotes.text: Unto him that receiveth I will give more.
we invoke the blessings of the Lord on you and your families, blessings of peace and contentment.
This is the restored gospel of Jesus Christ in His Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

scriptures.use: The source of the promise President Oaks quoted. Tell it in your own simple words during Open hands; an older child may read the verse aloud.
Have an older child read it aloud before One thing I will do, then ask what we should do after we hear God’s word.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Sikahema
aligned_quotes.text: What a blessing it is to live in a time when apostles and prophets are on the earth.

invitations.text: As the talks of this conference are published, we invite all to study and ponder them prayerfully and to act in faith on the principles they explain.

takeaways: The prophet invited me to learn from conference and do what I learn.
When I receive what Heavenly Father gives, He gives me more.
The temple is the house of the Lord, and the doors of the Salt Lake Temple will open to the public.
act: Listen to one conference talk or story with someone at home this week.
Say a prayer about what you heard.
Do the one thing you drew on your paper, and bring the paper back next week.
music: I Love to See the Temple

adapt.younger: Ages 3–7: use only two motions at first (open hands and marching), repeat the short truth after every activity, roll the ball instead of tossing it, and let helpers write each child’s choice on the back of the drawing. Shorten the talking and sing each song twice.
adapt.older: Ages 8–11: have a child read 2 Nephi 28:30 and James 1:22 aloud, let an older child lead the four actions game, and ask a harder question: why do you think Heavenly Father gives us a little at a time? Invite them to write the name of one conference talk they will listen to this week.
